title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer backoff and regional failover ordering to prevent thrashing
author: Amina Rahman
description:
Context: We observed a production incident where the SLO enforcer entered repeated backoff/re-enable cycles across regions under a bursty traffic pattern, which caused regional thrashing and excessive load-shedding. Root cause: the enforcer's backoff state was transient (in-memory) and the regional failover path could re-enable capacity out-of-order during partial recovery, allowing rapid toggles. This PR applies a targeted hotfix to prevent immediate re-enablement and add ordering guarantees to regional failover so nodes aren't re-added while global capacity is still unstable.

What I changed (single continuous description): Tighten the SLO enforcer backoff and gating: 1) persist enforcer backoff state to Redis so backoff survives scheduler restarts; 2) reduce aggressive immediate re-enable by enforcing a cooldown window and token-bucket rate (max_reenable_per_minute) with jitter; 3) add an ordering constraint in regional failover: prefer draining->quiesce->reenable with a global-coordinator checkpoint to avoid out-of-order readds; 4) add additional metrics (slo_enforcer.backoff_count, slo_enforcer.reenable_rate, slo_enforcer.persist_failures) and a SLI-friendly histogram for backoff durations; 5) add unit tests, simulate integration test that reproduces the thrash pattern in perf-canary, and tighten existing circuit-breaker invariants.

Why this is safe: Changes are localized to the SLO enforcer and regional failover flow. Persistence uses existing Redis cluster and falls back to in-memory on failure (with a metric). Default configuration keeps current defaults for most customers; the hotfix flips on a new feature flag by default in prod (slo_enforcer_global_backoff_v2=true) after canary verification. No API changes.

Testing and verification: Unit tests for backoff state machine and compare-and-swap race conditions added; integration test added to perf-canary which simulates 3-region burst and verifies no thrash after fix; ran a 2-hour soak on perf-canary with traffic ramp and observed stable reenable_rate below threshold and no >5% increased shed rate. CI: initial integration run showed a flaky timing assertion, adjusted tests to use wall-clock tolerant waits and re-ran (CI now green).

Deployment plan: 1) merge to main; 2) deploy enforcer service to staging behind feature flag; 3) enable in perf-canary and monitor metrics/alerts for 1 hour; 4) progressive rollout to prod regions over 30 minutes with an automated rollback if reenable_rate or shed_rate regress beyond threshold.

Related: ENG-6421 (postmortem/mitigation), SRE-1739 (runbook update), SUP-9843 (customer report).
